chapters.title: US Dollar
chapters.teaser: The dollar index edged up about 0.2% to near 101.8 in Asian trading, a quiet start to a week packed with US midterm elections on Tuesday and the October jobs report on Friday. Bets on a December Federal Reserve hike firmed slightly.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: High oil from the US–Iran war has kept US inflation well above the Federal Reserve's 2% goal. The Fed raised rates in September, then held on October 28 with two officials voting to hike, and two more officials have since called for further hikes. What changed: Over the weekend there was no US strike on Iran, and Iranian negotiators kept talking with Qatari mediators in Doha. Oil fell about 3%, but the dollar barely moved, edging up to near 101.8. Futures put a December hike at roughly 72–75%, up a touch from about 70% at Friday's close. What it means: Cheaper oil, if it lasts, would ease the inflation pressure that keeps the Fed leaning toward hikes. For now the dollar is waiting for harder evidence, so the question is whether the week's US data keeps the December hike alive.
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: the ISM survey of US factories at 9:00 AM CT today, the US midterm elections on Tuesday, the ISM services survey at 9:00 AM CT Wednesday, and the October jobs report at 7:30 AM CT Friday. The next Fed decision is December 9.

scenarios.bull: A strong factory survey and firmer hike bets lift yields; the index climbs above 102.3.
scenarios.bear: Oil keeps falling on hopes of a Doha deal and hike bets fade; the index slips below 101.3.

chapters.title: Euro
chapters.teaser: The euro held near $1.117, close to its weakest in about 17 months. Fitch cut its outlook on France's credit rating to negative late Friday, adding to the weight on the euro before euro-area inflation figures on Wednesday.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Energy costs have pushed euro-area inflation well above the European Central Bank's 2% goal, and the ECB held rates on October 29 while pointing to a hike in December. France's budget trouble and a slowing economy keep the euro under pressure. What changed: Fitch Ratings moved France's outlook to negative late on Friday, warning of a possible downgrade as debt keeps climbing and politics make cuts hard. Germany also started winter with gas stores short of target as a cold snap arrived. Cheaper oil overnight helps a region that buys most of its energy abroad, but it was not enough to lift the euro. What it means: Two of the three big rating firms now have France on negative watch, which keeps a risk premium on the euro even as an ECB hike looks likely. The question is whether Wednesday's inflation figure firms up the December hike enough to outweigh French debt worries.
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: France's parliament votes on the revenue part of its budget on Tuesday, euro-area inflation for October at 4:00 AM CT Wednesday (forecast 4.0%), and a speech by ECB President Christine Lagarde Thursday at noon CT.

chapters.title: British Pound
chapters.teaser: The pound held near $1.339, steady after a strong Friday. Markets still see a Bank of England rate hike on Thursday, November 5, as all but certain, so the debate is whether it hints at another in December.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: UK inflation rose to 3.5% in September, its highest in about a year, driven by energy and fuel. The UK Budget passed calmly on October 28, leaving the pound trading on interest rates. What changed: Little overnight; the pound slipped slightly against a firmer dollar but held near its strongest against the euro this year. Market pricing still puts a Thursday hike to 4.00% at about 94%. What it means: With the hike itself nearly fully expected, the pound will move on the message: a hint of a second hike in December would support it, while a hike framed as one-and-done could let it slip.
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: the Bank of England decision and its Monetary Policy Report at 6:00 AM CT Thursday, November 5. Before that, UK business surveys this week and the US jobs report Friday.
numbers: EUR/GBP ~0.834, near its lowest in about 19 months

scenarios.bull: A hike plus a clear hint of December; the pound rises above $1.346.
scenarios.bear: A hike framed as the last for now, or a split vote leaning dovish; the pound falls below $1.333.

chapters.title: Japanese Yen
chapters.teaser: The dollar edged up to about ¥157.8 in Asian trading as calm markets reduced demand for the safe-haven yen. A December Bank of Japan hike is still expected, but Governor Kazuo Ueda has given no date.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Japanese rates are far below those of other major economies, and high oil costs Japan money, which has kept the yen weak. The Bank of Japan held at 1.25% on October 30 but said underlying inflation has reached its 2% goal, pointing toward a December hike. What changed: Share markets started November on a firmer note after October's tech sell-off, so investors had less reason to hold the yen for safety. Cheaper oil helps Japan's import bill, but the wide gap with US rates still dominated. What it means: The yen needs either a clear signal from the Bank of Japan or lower US yields to gain much ground. Tokyo's warnings about sharp moves still limit how weak it gets. The question is whether US data this week widens or narrows the rate gap.
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: the US factory survey at 9:00 AM CT today, the US midterms on Tuesday, the US jobs report at 7:30 AM CT Friday, and a speech by Governor Kazuo Ueda at 10:00 AM CT Friday. The next Bank of Japan decision is December 18.
numbers: Bank of Japan rate 1.25%; December hike ~80% priced

chapters.title: Swiss Franc
chapters.teaser: The franc was little changed near 0.824 per dollar overnight. Swiss inflation figures for October come at 1:30 AM CT Tuesday and are expected to show prices flat on the month.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Swiss inflation is low, so the Swiss National Bank holds its rate at zero and has said it is less ready to fight a weaker franc. The franc mostly moves on the global mood. What changed: Nothing Swiss overnight. Firmer share markets and cheaper oil gave investors little reason to seek safety, so the franc drifted slightly weaker. What it means: A soft inflation reading on Tuesday would keep talk of a Swiss rate cut alive, which tends to weigh on the franc; a firm one would ease that. The question is whether markets stay calm enough to keep the franc's safety demand low.
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: Swiss inflation for October at 1:30 AM CT Tuesday (forecast 0.0% on the month), and a speech by Swiss National Bank Chairman Martin Schlegel at 6:40 AM CT Thursday. The next decision is December 10.

chapters.title: Australian Dollar
chapters.teaser: The Aussie slipped slightly to about 70.2 US cents before the Reserve Bank of Australia decision at 9:30 PM CT tonight. Markets put the chance of a hike to 4.85%, the highest since 2008, at roughly 80–90%.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Australian inflation ran hotter than the Reserve Bank of Australia expected over the summer, and the bank has raised rates four times this year. A weakening job market is the main drag. What changed: China's private factory survey beat forecasts at 52.0, softening Saturday's weak official reading, though export orders grew at their slowest in three months. Cheaper oil trimmed some of the lift Australia gets from high energy prices. A Reuters poll found 30 of 32 economists expect a hike tonight. What it means: The hike itself is mostly expected, so the Aussie will move on what Governor Michele Bullock signals about more. Some economists think a confirmed hike could lift the Aussie because the RBA seems more willing to keep going than New Zealand's central bank.
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: the RBA decision at 9:30 PM CT tonight, then Governor Michele Bullock's press conference at 10:30 PM CT. The US jobs report follows at 7:30 AM CT Friday.
numbers: Reuters poll: 30 of 32 economists expect a hike

scenarios.bull: A hike with a clear hint of more; the Aussie rises above 70.6 cents.
scenarios.bear: A surprise hold; the Aussie falls below 69.5 cents.

chapters.title: Canadian Dollar
chapters.teaser: The loonie weakened to about 1.399 per US dollar as US crude fell about 3% to near $100.50 a barrel. On Sunday, President Donald Trump said the US and Canada are very close to a trade deal, though no terms were given.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: The Bank of Canada raised rates to 2.50% on October 28 as energy lifted inflation, but the economy has not grown since June. High oil prices have helped the loonie. What changed: Oil fell overnight on hopes for the Doha talks, taking away some of that support. Trump said a US–Canada trade deal is very close and Prime Minister Mark Carney described the talks as constructive, but nothing has been signed. What it means: Cheaper oil weakens the loonie's main prop, while a real trade deal would remove a long-running drag on Canadian business. The question is which arrives first: a lasting fall in oil or a signed deal.
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: Bank of Canada governor Tiff Macklem speaks at 10:00 AM CT Tuesday and 9:30 AM CT Thursday, Canada's federal budget lands at 3:00 PM CT Thursday, and Canada's October jobs report comes at 7:30 AM CT Friday.
numbers: December Bank of Canada hike ~45% priced

scenarios.bull: A signed trade deal or oil back above $105; the US dollar falls below 1.392 loonies.
scenarios.bear: WTI below $97 on a Doha deal; the US dollar rises above 1.405 loonies.

chapters.title: New Zealand Dollar
chapters.teaser: The kiwi fell about 0.4% to near 56.2 US cents, the weakest of the majors overnight. New Zealand votes in a general election on Saturday, November 7, and its job figures come out Tuesday afternoon CT.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand surprised markets by holding at 2.75% on October 28, though all its members said more tightening is likely. Unemployment sits near a decade high. What changed: Election nerves added to the pressure. Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's National-led coalition faces voter anger over living costs and jobs, and the opposition Labour Party wants to restore the central bank's employment mandate. Markets still price about a 75% chance of a December hike. What it means: Strong job figures would firm up a December hike and support the kiwi. Commonwealth Bank of Australia expects a National-led win to lift the kiwi modestly, and a Labour-Green government to weigh on it if debt worries grow.
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: New Zealand's job figures for July to September at 3:45 PM CT Tuesday (forecast: jobs +0.4%, unemployment 5.5%), then the election on Saturday, November 7. The next RBNZ decision is December 9.

scenarios.bear: Weak hiring or election worries deepen; the kiwi falls below 55.6 cents.

chapters.title: Oil
chapters.teaser: Brent fell about 3% to near $110 a barrel in Asian trading as Iranian negotiators held a third day of talks with Qatari mediators in Doha. A tanker hit by two projectiles off Saudi Arabia did not stop the slide.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: The US–Iran war and a US blockade of Iranian oil have kept prices high, with attacks on Gulf shipping and Saudi oil sites adding a risk premium. What changed: The weekend passed with no US strike, and the Doha talks reportedly include a possible plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz if Washington cooperates. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said no decision on strikes has been made and he prefers diplomacy. OPEC+ left its December output targets unchanged. A tanker was hit off the Saudi coast early Monday, part of about ten Gulf shipping incidents in three days. What it means: Hope for a deal is draining some of the war premium, even as attacks on ships continue. Lower oil would ease inflation pressure worldwide and weigh on oil exporters' currencies such as the Canadian dollar.
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: any outcome from the Doha talks and the US midterm elections on Tuesday, after reports that the US told Gulf allies to brace for a short campaign against Iran once the vote is over.
numbers: ~10 Gulf shipping incidents in three days

scenarios.bull: Talks stall or a big attack hits Gulf supply; Brent rises above $115.
scenarios.bear: A Hormuz reopening plan is agreed; Brent falls below $105.

chapters.title: Gold
chapters.teaser: Gold rose about 0.6% to near $3,907 an ounce in Asian trading, a small bounce after last week's slide to a one-year low. Cheaper oil eased some of the inflation fear that has pushed bets on higher rates.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Gold has fallen hard since October, hit by bets that central banks will keep raising rates to fight energy-driven inflation, and by selling to cover stock losses during a tech slide. What changed: Share markets steadied and oil fell overnight, which slightly lowered the odds of runaway inflation and gave gold room to recover a little. Bets on a December Fed hike still edged up. What it means: Gold is caught between two pulls: higher US rates make it less attractive, while any return of war or market fear brings buyers back. Hedge funds still hold big bets on gold, though they have been cutting them. The question is whether this week's US data pushes hike bets up or down.
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: the US factory survey at 9:00 AM CT today, the US midterms on Tuesday, and the US jobs report at 7:30 AM CT Friday.

calls.text: US 10-year yield below 5% after the tech sell-off: if Asian and European stocks keep falling overnight, the yen pushes toward ¥156 and the dollar index slips under 101.5; a rebound in stocks lifts yields and the dollar back toward ¥157.5
calls.note: Asian stocks kept falling (Nikkei −1.3%) and the dollar dipped to about ¥156.3, but steadied near ¥156.9 by 12:40 AM CT; the dollar index held at about 101.5 rather than slipping under it.

calls.text: Euro-area flash business surveys Fri 3:00 AM CT (manufacturing ~52.7, services ~52.6 expected), hours before Moody's on France: misses keep the euro near $1.12; beats firm December ECB hike bets and lift it
calls.note: The surveys missed (euro-area composite 51.9, France back in contraction at 48.4), and the euro stayed near $1.12.

calls.text: US flash PMIs Fri 8:45 AM CT (services ~58.0 expected) and Michigan inflation expectations 9:00 AM CT: firm readings lift yields back toward 5% and steady the dollar; soft ones extend the bond rally
calls.note: The surveys were firm on prices and the Michigan inflation outlook ticked up; the 10-year yield rose back to about 5.00% and the dollar index firmed to about 101.8 on Friday.

calls.text: SNB policy summary 2:30 AM CT: worry about a strong franc keeps December cut bets alive and caps the franc; a calmer tone lets it firm
calls.note: Calmer tone: the bank dropped its stronger readiness to intervene and gave no December cut signal. The franc firmed slightly, with the dollar near 0.823, and hit a three-month high against the euro.

calls.text: Saudi departure order: widening across the Gulf or a hit on Saudi output puts Brent well above $110 and lifts the dollar and loonie; staying contained lets oil drift
calls.note: Brent did climb well above $110 (about $113 by the close), but on reports of US–Israeli strike plans and Iranian tanker claims, not a wider departure order. The loonie edged up; the dollar slipped.

calls.text: UK retail sales Fri 1:00 AM CT (−0.2% expected): a strong print lifts December hike bets and the pound; a weak one trims both
calls.note: Sales fell 0.4%, worse than expected, yet the pound reached its strongest against the euro since May 2025 on Friday as a November Bank of England hike stayed near certain.

calls.text: US jobless claims Thu 7:30 AM CT (about 200,000 expected): staying low keeps the Fed's December hike near 90%; a jump trims it and weighs on the dollar
calls.note: Claims stayed low at 194,000 (200,000 expected), near their lowest in decades. December hike bets held near 90% (CME FedWatch, Oct 21); a sharp bond rally later still pulled the dollar lower.

calls.text: Moody's review of France Fri: a downgrade widens France's gap over German yields and weighs on the euro; holding the rating eases the pressure
calls.note: Moody's held France at Aa3; French yields eased on Monday and the euro led the majors in the European morning.

calls.text: Bailey 8:00 AM CT after the 3.5% UK inflation print: backing November without promising more keeps the pound near $1.34; any opening to a December follow-up lifts it; calling energy temporary trims it
calls.note: Neither branch: Bailey gave no new signal on rates. The pound still held near $1.34 (about 1.3395 at the New York close), with December's second hike about a coin toss.

calls.text: US crude oil stocks 9:30 AM CT (industry survey: about −4.9M barrels): a big official draw keeps Brent above $110; a build lets the rebound fade
calls.note: The draw came (−3.1M barrels, far more than forecast) and Brent briefly topped $110.8, but it still faded to $108.82 at the settle after the US Treasury's tanker licence and emergency fuel loans.

calls.text: Pakistan's mediation after Iran's uranium refusal: any confirmed opening drains oil's premium and lifts the euro and yen; more warships and no talks keep Brent near $110 into the close
calls.note: No opening: Rubio called a deal extremely difficult and more US warships headed in. Brent settled at $108.82, near $110 but off its high on Washington's supply moves rather than diplomacy.

calls.text: Japan national CPI Thu 6:30 PM CT (2.1% expected): a hot print keeps the BoJ's December hike near three in four; a soft one fades it and weighs on the yen
calls.note: Neither branch: 2.1% exactly as expected (1.7% prior), though the measure that also leaves out energy jumped to 2.4%. December hike pricing held near 80%.

calls.text: US–Iran framework: confirmation by either government drains oil's risk premium and pulls US long yields lower; another denial puts Brent back toward $110
calls.note: No confirmation from either government, and no fresh denial either. Brent still climbed back toward $110 overnight, on tanker attacks spreading to the Gulf of Oman rather than on the talks.

calls.text: RBA's Hauser 5:30 PM CT: leaning on sticky inflation keeps a November hike near 1 in 3; leaning on the softer job market trims it
calls.note: Hauser leaned on sticky inflation: the outlook is 'materially worse'. Odds of a November hike rose to about 40% from about 30%, and the Aussie hit a three-week high near 0.702.

calls.text: China Q3 GDP 4.5% vs 4.4% fc — the aussie's demand read
calls.note: Beat: 4.5% vs 4.4% fc (q/q 1.2%); retail +1.1% the standout. AUD/USD +0.3-0.5% to ~0.697, the night's best G10 performer; USD/CNH 6.6811, strongest since June 2022. Two-speed beat (factories lead, property -20.6% YTD).

calls.text: Petersburg Oil Terminal drone strike — Baltic supply risk into Monday's open vs the waiver's lower-price pull
calls.note: Fire CONFIRMED (Beglov; Fire Point confirmed its FP-1 hit the terminal); ~1 killed, several injured (figures vary); damage extent still unquantified. Crude's Sunday open came flat — neither the spike nor the tumble; Asia Brent -1.0 to -1.8%.

calls.text: Beirut strike fallout: the haven-bid tell at Monday's open
calls.note: No Hezbollah retaliation as of Monday's open (Qmati: strike crossed a 'red line', leadership to decide; IDF: normal routines). Haven bid stayed sheathed — DXY flat 101.80-101.83, havens ~flat in Asia. The tell held: no escalation, no haven extension.

calls.text: October FOMC priced as a hold (~85%) into the Saturday blackout; December is the live debate
Brent broke $108 on Ukraine refinery strikes — $105-112 range into the weekend (prior $104-108 call broken)
USD/CAD holds 1.41-1.43 into the BoC (Oct 28); Canada CPI Mon the trigger
calls.note: Oct 19: CPI passed without a break — USD/CAD ~1.411 at the NY close, still inside the range. Runs to the Oct 28 decision. Oct 20: dipped to ~1.409, a hair under the floor, as oil and BoC hike bets lifted the loonie. Oct 20 close: broke below the floor — USD/CAD ~1.406, strongest loonie since Sep 22, on BoC hike pricing (~80–85%) and Alberta's vote to remain.
The tripwire never bit — Friday's waiver suspends the duties outright with no end date. Superseded by the ~Dec 17 60-day review clock.
calls.text: Graham Act Oct-18 tripwire: waivers extended or enforcement begins — oil's Sunday open is the tell
Iran deal Sunday signing: Trump's 'OPEN TO ALL' vs Tehran's 'not tomorrow' — the strait itself is the verdict
calls.note: No signed deal carried by any major wire by 4pm CT Sunday; Trump's 'complete' claim stands unverified against Tehran's 'talks stalled'. Aggregator 'markets celebrate' content held — its futures numbers contradict Friday's verified settles. The signing test is claim day, not done day.

calls.text: Canada CPI Mon 7:30am CT (TD 3.2%, UBS 3.3%, RBC 3.0%): hot (3.3%+) revives the Oct 28 hike; soft (3.0%-) buries it to December
calls.note: Neither branch: 3.1% vs 3.2% expected, core measures cooled to 1.8–1.9%. October stayed about 1 in 4 (a hold), with about one quarter-point hike priced by December; consumers' inflation expectations rose to ~3.9% in the BoC survey. Correction (Oct 20): by Monday's close swaps had jumped to ~87% for an October hike on Macklem's Saturday forecast warning; the 1-in-4 figure was stale.

calls.text: UK CPI Wed 1am CT (3.4% fc vs 3.1%): 3.5%+ starts pricing a December follow-up; soft reopens Bailey's 2027 read
calls.note: Hot branch: 3.5% vs 3.4% expected (3.1% in August), the highest in 11 months. November's hike is near certain; how much December moved was not yet verified at write.

calls.text: NZ Q3 CPI Wed 4:45pm CT (ANZ 3.8% y/y): hot settles the RBNZ's two-way bet toward the hike side
calls.note: Not hot: inflation came in at 3.7%, a touch soft. The hike side still settled anyway, with October 28 now about 98% priced.

calls.text: Japan CPI Fri + BoJ Oct 29-30: Ueda's 'quite close' language tested — October hike stays ~25%
calls.note: Oct 19: swaps now put an October 30 hike under 5% (BBH), below the ~25% in the call. December ~80% unchanged. October hike odds fell to about 4%, far below the ~25% in the call; Japan's inflation came in at 2.1% as expected and December (~80%) is now the meeting that matters.

calls.text: France's revenue-section budget vote Tue: a clean pass narrows the French–German spread (~141bp); a defeat or big concessions widens it and weighs on the euro
calls.note: No vote on Tuesday: it was pushed to October 27, so neither branch played out.

calls.text: UK jobs Tue 1 AM CT (earnings ~3.8% expected): sticky pay firms the BoE hike case before Wednesday's inflation; cooling pay backs Bailey's calmer view
calls.note: Sticky side won: unemployment fell to 4.7% (4.9% expected) and regular pay rose 3.7% (3.6% expected); total pay and claims were softer. Pound +0.3% to ~1.334.

calls.text: Konarak follow-through: a US confirmation or more strikes keeps oil's supply premium and lifts US yields; silence lets the morning's waiver drop resume
calls.note: No confirmation (a US official denied the strike) and no new strike overnight, yet the premium held: Brent ~$109.8 Tuesday on low Gulf flows and Iran's Hormuz claims. The waiver-driven drop did not resume.

calls.text: BoC Oct 28 with ~87% priced for a hike: a hike is mostly in the loonie already; a hold would be the surprise and hit it
calls.note: The Bank of Canada hiked as priced, and the loonie barely moved on the day.

calls.text: NZ Q3 CPI Wed 4:45pm CT (~3.8% y/y): near forecast keeps the ~80% hike pricing; clearly soft reopens the hold and weighs on the kiwi
calls.note: Near forecast (3.7% vs 3.8%) and hike pricing held, rising to about 98%; the kiwi dipped only briefly.
